report:
## Conclusion

The claim is **true and well-supported**: abaloparatide reduces vertebral fracture risk in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

## Evidence

The primary evidence comes from the pivotal **ACTIVE trial** (Abaloparatide Comparator Trial In Vertebral Endpoints), a randomized, double-blind, placebo- and teriparatide-controlled study of 2,463 postmenopausal women (mean age 69). Published in JAMA, it found that 18 months of daily subcutaneous abaloparatide significantly reduced new morphometric vertebral fractures compared to placebo (0.6% vs. 4.2%), along with reductions in nonvertebral fractures ([jamanetwork.com](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640); [pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27533157](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27533157/?dopt=Abstract)).

This trial formed the basis of **FDA approval** (2017). The official FDA label confirms the same finding: 0.6% vertebral fracture incidence with abaloparatide vs. 4.2% with placebo (p<0.0001) ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf)).

Subsequent analyses reinforce this conclusion. A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis in *ScienceDirect* concluded abaloparatide reduces vertebral fracture risk while increasing bone mineral density at the spine, femoral neck, and hip, with a favorable safety profile ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0149291824000043)). A more recent 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis (MDPI) similarly found abaloparatide provides "strong vertebral protection" with moderate-certainty evidence for nonvertebral effects ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0383/15/2/673)).

Comparative data further support efficacy: a network meta-analysis and a head-to-head trial versus alendronate both indicate abaloparatide may produce even greater vertebral fracture reduction than active bisphosphonate comparators ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31674644](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31674644/)).

## Bottom Line

Multiple independent lines of evidence—a large RCT, FDA regulatory review, and multiple meta-analyses—consistently confirm that abaloparatide significantly reduces vertebral fracture risk in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.
